periods.title: Ferry Arrival & Ojo de Agua
periods.text: Take the early ferry from San Jorge (near Rivas) across Lake Nicaragua to Moyogalpa on Ometepe's western shore. The 1-hour crossing gives you your first view of the twin volcanoes: Concepción's perfect cone rising to 1,610m on the left and the forested dome of Maderas (1,394m) on the right. From Moyogalpa, rent a scooter or take a taxi to Ojo de Agua, a pair of natural spring-fed swimming pools surrounded by tropical gardens. The crystal-clear water is cool, refreshing, and mineral-rich.
periods.tip: Ferries from San Jorge leave hourly from 7am. The early ferries are less crowded. Bring your passport, as you may be checked.

periods.title: Cycling the Island Road
periods.text: Rent a bicycle and ride the road that circles the isthmus connecting the two volcanoes. The flat stretch between Ojo de Agua and the village of Altagracia passes through farmland, banana plantations, and small communities. Stop at the pre-Columbian petroglyph museum in Altagracia where carved stone statues depicting gods and animals line the path of the village park.
periods.tip: The road is paved but rough in places. A mountain bike is better than a road bike. Bring plenty of water, as shade is scarce on the isthmus.

periods.title: Sunset Between Two Volcanoes
periods.text: Find a spot on the isthmus between the two volcanoes, ideally Playa Santo Domingo, and watch the sun set over Lake Nicaragua with Concepción's silhouette against the fading sky. The beach is made of dark volcanic sand and the water is warm and calm. Eat dinner at one of the simple beach restaurants on fresh lake fish with plantain and rice.
periods.tip: Playa Santo Domingo has several budget hostels and restaurants right on the beach. It is the best base for exploring the island.

3.title: Arrival, Ojo de Agua & Charco Verde

periods.title: Ferry to Ometepe & Orientation
periods.text: Catch the early ferry from San Jorge across Lake Nicaragua to Moyogalpa. The hour-long crossing reveals the full majesty of Ometepe's twin volcanoes rising from the lake like a figure-eight sculpture. At Moyogalpa, rent a scooter ($15–20/day) or arrange onward transport. Head east along the main road toward the isthmus, stopping to admire the views as Concepción's perfectly symmetrical cone towers above the surrounding farmland.
periods.tip: Rent a scooter in Moyogalpa, as the island is too spread out for walking and taxis are expensive. A scooter gives you complete freedom for about $15–20 per day including fuel.

periods.title: Charco Verde & Monkey Island
periods.text: Ride to the Reserva Natural Charco Verde on Concepción's southern flank, a green lagoon surrounded by forest that is home to howler monkeys, parrots, and butterflies. Walk the short nature trail (1.5km, 45 minutes) that loops around the lagoon through dense tropical vegetation. Then take a short boat ride to Monkey Island (Isla de los Monos), a tiny island inhabited by a troop of spider monkeys who swing through the trees and sometimes approach visitors.
periods.tip: The Charco Verde entrance fee is about 100 córdobas. Monkey Island boats leave from the nearby shore and cost about $5 per person.

periods.title: Ojo de Agua Natural Springs
periods.text: End the afternoon at Ojo de Agua, two natural spring-fed pools of crystal-clear water surrounded by tropical gardens with a rope swing and diving platform. The water emerges from underground volcanic springs at a cool, refreshing temperature that is heavenly after a day of exploring in the heat. Stay for sunset drinks at the adjacent bar, then ride to your accommodation on Playa Santo Domingo.
periods.tip: Ojo de Agua entry costs about 100 córdobas. Visit in the late afternoon when day-trippers have left and you may have the pools almost to yourself.

periods.title: Climbing Volcán Concepción
periods.text: Start before dawn for the gruelling but spectacular hike up Volcán Concepción, a near-perfect 1,610m volcanic cone and Ometepe's dominant landmark. A mandatory local guide leads you through farmland, then dense forest, then increasingly exposed volcanic rock and scree. The final push to the crater rim involves scrambling over loose rocks with views expanding in every direction: the entire lake, the island of Maderas, and on clear days, the volcanoes of Costa Rica to the south.
periods.tip: This is a serious 8–10 hour hike with 1,400m of elevation gain. Start at 4–5am, bring 3+ litres of water, snacks, sun protection, and layers for the cold windy summit. A guide is legally required and costs about $25 USD.

periods.title: Summit & Descent
periods.text: The crater rim of Concepción is often shrouded in cloud, but if you are lucky and arrive early enough, the clouds part to reveal a dizzying view down into the steaming crater. The descent is steep and hard on the knees but faster. Most hikers are back at the trailhead by early afternoon, exhausted but exhilarated. The sense of achievement from standing on top of this island volcano in the middle of a lake is immense.
periods.tip: Bring trekking poles if you have them, as the descent is steep and slippery. Gaiters or long socks help keep volcanic gravel out of your shoes.

periods.title: Recovery & Beach Sunset
periods.text: After the biggest hike of your trip, collapse on Playa Santo Domingo and watch the sunset paint the lake in orange and gold. Treat yourself to a large dinner, because you have earned it. Cold beer, fresh fish, rice and beans, and the satisfaction of having climbed one of Nicaragua's most impressive volcanoes.
periods.tip: Your legs will be sore tomorrow. Ojo de Agua's mineral springs are perfect for post-hike recovery, so plan a relaxed morning.

periods.title: Pre-Columbian Petroglyphs
periods.text: Explore Ometepe's ancient petroglyphs, carved stone artworks created by the Nahuatl and Chorotega peoples who inhabited the island over 1,000 years ago. The best-preserved examples are found near the village of Altagracia (in the park and museum) and scattered through the farmland on the Maderas side of the island. The carvings depict spirals, jaguars, monkeys, and human figures, and their exact meaning remains debated by archaeologists.
periods.tip: The Altagracia museum is small but fascinating, with stone statues and carved figures displayed in the village park. Entry is free or a small donation.

periods.title: Lake Kayaking
periods.text: Rent a kayak at Playa Santo Domingo and paddle along the shore of the isthmus with both volcanoes framing the horizon. The lake water is warm and usually calm near the shore. Paddle south toward the Maderas side to spot herons, cormorants, and possibly freshwater turtles. The views of both volcanoes reflected in the still lake are extraordinary.
periods.tip: Kayak rental costs about $5–8 per hour. Morning is usually calmest, as afternoon winds can pick up on the lake.

periods.title: Ferry Departure
periods.text: Catch a late afternoon ferry back to San Jorge for onward travel. The sunset crossing is beautiful, with the twin volcanoes receding into silhouette as the lake turns gold. From San Jorge, buses connect to Rivas (10 minutes), the Costa Rica border at Peñas Blancas (45 minutes), San Juan del Sur (1 hour), and Managua (2 hours).
periods.tip: Check the ferry schedule the day before, as the last ferry is usually around 5:30pm. Missing it means an unplanned night on the island (not the worst fate).

periods.title: Ferry to Ometepe
periods.text: Take the early ferry from San Jorge to Moyogalpa. Watch the twin volcanoes emerge from the lake haze as you approach. At the port, rent a scooter ($15–20/day) and ride east along the main road. Stop at viewpoints along the way as Concepción's cone grows ever more imposing.
periods.tip: Bring your passport for the ferry. Arrive 30 minutes early for the first crossing to ensure space for your scooter.

periods.title: Settle In & Explore the Isthmus
periods.text: Head to Playa Santo Domingo and check into your accommodation. Spend the afternoon exploring the isthmus, the narrow strip connecting the two volcanic halves of the island. The dark sand beach stretches along the eastern shore with calm, warm lake water and views of both volcanoes.
periods.tip: Playa Santo Domingo has the best range of budget accommodation and restaurants. It is the ideal base for the week.

periods.title: First Sunset on Ometepe
periods.text: Watch your first Ometepe sunset from the beach. The sun drops behind Concepción's silhouette while the sky turns from gold to crimson reflected in the lake. Dine at a beachfront restaurant on fresh tilapia from the lake with fried plantain.
periods.tip: Electricity on Ometepe can be unreliable, so bring a headlamp and a portable charger.

periods.title: Charco Verde Nature Reserve
periods.text: Ride to Charco Verde and walk the nature trail that loops around the green lagoon. Howler monkeys crash through the canopy above, parrots squawk from the treetops, and butterflies cluster at the water's edge. The reserve is small but biodiversity-rich and peaceful.
periods.tip: Bring binoculars for birdwatching. The early morning is best for wildlife, as howler monkeys are most active around dawn.

periods.title: Monkey Island Boat Trip
periods.text: Take a boat from near Charco Verde to Monkey Island, a tiny island inhabited by a troop of spider monkeys. The monkeys are semi-wild and accustomed to visitors, swinging through the trees and occasionally approaching boats. The boat ride also passes other small islands with bird colonies.
periods.tip: Do not feed the monkeys, as it disrupts their diet and behaviour. Keep belongings secure as they are curious and will grab anything shiny.

periods.title: Ojo de Agua Evening Swim
periods.text: Cool off at Ojo de Agua's natural springs in the late afternoon when it is quietest. The rope swing and diving platform add fun, and the mineral-rich water soothes tired muscles. Stay for drinks at the bar as the light fades through the tropical gardens.
periods.tip: Ojo de Agua closes at 5pm most days. Arrive by 3pm to enjoy a couple of unhurried hours.

periods.title: Pre-Dawn Start
periods.text: Meet your mandatory guide at 4–5am for the hike up Volcán Concepción. The trail climbs through farmland and into dense forest, then emerges onto exposed volcanic rock and scree. The 1,400m elevation gain over 8–10 hours is gruelling but the views from the crater rim are extraordinary: the entire lake, Maderas, and on clear days the volcanoes of Costa Rica.
periods.tip: Pack 3+ litres of water, energy snacks, sun protection, warm layers for the summit, and trekking poles. This is the hardest day hike in Nicaragua.

periods.title: Summit & Return
periods.text: Reach the crater rim and peer into the steaming vent if the clouds cooperate. The descent is steep and punishing on tired legs but faster than the ascent. Most groups return to the trailhead by 2–3pm. The sense of achievement is immense.
periods.tip: Start as early as possible, as the summit clouds over by mid-morning most days. The earlier you reach the top, the better your chances of a clear view.

periods.title: Post-Hike Recovery
periods.text: Collapse at your accommodation and treat yourself to the biggest dinner available. Your body needs fuel and rest. Watch the sunset from a horizontal position. You have earned every second of relaxation.
periods.tip: Ice is available at most restaurants, so ask for a bag to reduce knee and ankle swelling. Tomorrow should be a rest day.

periods.title: Sleep In & Slow Morning
periods.text: Let your body recover from yesterday's volcano. Sleep late, eat a big breakfast, and stretch your aching muscles. Walk to the beach for a gentle swim in the warm lake water, as the buoyancy helps sore legs.
periods.tip: Visit Ojo de Agua again this morning. The mineral springs are genuinely therapeutic for post-hike muscle soreness.

periods.title: Hammock & Reading Time
periods.text: Embrace the pace of island life. Spend the afternoon in a hammock with a book, or rent a kayak for a gentle paddle along the shore. The views of both volcanoes from the water are constantly changing as clouds build and dissipate around the summits.
periods.tip: Most hostels have free kayaks or can arrange rental for about $5 per hour. Stick to the calm morning water.

periods.title: Stargazing
periods.text: Ometepe has minimal light pollution and the night sky is spectacular. Lie on the beach after dinner and watch the Milky Way arc between the two volcano silhouettes. If you are lucky, you will see shooting stars and the bright band of the galaxy reflected in the still lake.
periods.tip: New moon periods offer the best stargazing. Even during brighter phases, the sky quality here is far superior to mainland cities.

periods.title: Hike to Cascada San Ramón
periods.text: Take on a gentler hike today: the trail to Cascada San Ramón on the southern flank of Volcán Maderas. The 4km path climbs through coffee plantations and cloud forest to a 50m waterfall that plunges down a moss-covered cliff into a natural pool. The hike takes 2–3 hours round trip and is far less demanding than Concepción.
periods.tip: The trail can be muddy, so wear proper shoes with grip. The waterfall is most impressive in or just after the rainy season.

periods.title: Finca Magdalena Coffee Tour
periods.text: Near the Maderas trailhead, Finca Magdalena is a cooperative coffee farm that also operates as a hostel. Take a guided tour of the coffee operation, from plant to cup, and taste the beans grown on Maderas' volcanic slopes. The finca also has some of the best-preserved petroglyphs on the island, carved into boulders scattered through the farm.
periods.tip: The coffee tour costs about $5 and includes a tasting. Buy a bag of beans directly from the cooperative, the freshest and cheapest you will find.

periods.title: Quiet Night at Finca Magdalena
periods.text: Consider staying overnight at Finca Magdalena for a completely different island experience. The hostel is basic but atmospheric, with hammocks on the porch, fireflies in the garden, and the sounds of the forest at night. Dinner is home-cooked Nicaraguan food from the farm kitchen.
periods.tip: Dorm beds at Finca Magdalena cost about $6. The lack of WiFi and phone signal is a feature, not a bug.

periods.title: Ancient Petroglyphs Trail
periods.text: Explore the pre-Columbian petroglyphs scattered across the Maderas side of the island. The Altagracia museum displays carved stone statues in the village park, while more examples are found along farm trails and in forest clearings. These carvings are over 1,000 years old and depict spirals, animals, and human figures.
periods.tip: Hire a local guide in Altagracia to find the less-visited petroglyphs on private farmland. Costs about $10 and is far more rewarding than the museum alone.

periods.title: Cycling the Island
periods.text: Rent a bicycle and ride the road around the Concepción side of the island. The route passes through farming villages, banana plantations, and volcanic viewpoints. Stop at roadside stands for fresh fruit and cold drinks. The flat sections along the isthmus are easy, while the hills near the volcano base provide a workout.
periods.tip: The full loop around Concepción is about 30km. The road is paved but rough, so a mountain bike is essential. Start early to avoid the midday heat.

periods.title: Final Beach Sunset
periods.text: Return to Playa Santo Domingo for your last full evening on the island. Swim in the warm lake, watch the sunset between the volcanoes, and reflect on a week spent in one of the most unique landscapes in Central America. Toast the island with a rum at the beach bar.
periods.tip: Pack your bag tonight for an early departure tomorrow. Check the ferry schedule, as the first morning ferry is the most reliable.

periods.title: Sunrise Kayak
periods.text: Wake early for a final sunrise kayak paddle along the shore. The lake is perfectly still at dawn and both volcanoes are reflected in the mirror-like water. Watch fishermen in their small wooden boats setting nets as the sky turns gold. This is Ometepe at its most peaceful and beautiful.
periods.tip: Return your scooter with a full tank to avoid extra charges. Allow 30 minutes for the ride from Santo Domingo to Moyogalpa.

periods.title: Ferry & Onward Travel
periods.text: Take a late morning ferry back to San Jorge. The crossing gives you a final look at the twin volcanoes receding into the distance. From San Jorge, connect to Rivas (10 minutes), then onward to Costa Rica (Peñas Blancas border, 45 minutes), San Juan del Sur (1 hour), Granada (2 hours), or Managua (2 hours).
periods.tip: The Costa Rica border crossing at Peñas Blancas can take 1–2 hours. Bring exact change for exit and entry fees ($3 exit from Nicaragua, $13 entry to Costa Rica).

periods.title: Next Destination
periods.text: Arrive at your next destination with memories of an island unlike anywhere else. Ometepe's combination of twin volcanoes, ancient petroglyphs, natural springs, and lake life creates an experience that stays with travellers long after they leave.
periods.tip: If heading to Costa Rica, La Fortuna and Santa Teresa are excellent next stops. Both offer different flavours of Central American adventure.

budgetTips.title: Rent a scooter
budgetTips.text: Scooters cost $15–20 per day and are the most practical way to explore the island. Taxis are expensive due to the distances. Cycling is possible but the heat and hills make it exhausting for long distances.

budgetTips.title: Stay at fincas
budgetTips.text: Working farms like Finca Magdalena and Finca El Porvenir offer dorm beds for $5–8 per night with home-cooked meals. They are more atmospheric than hotels and directly support the local community.

budgetTips.title: Cook your own food
budgetTips.text: Buy supplies at small shops in Moyogalpa or Altagracia. Many hostels have kitchens. Market fruit (mangoes, bananas, papayas) is practically free on the island.

budgetTips.title: Group volcano hike
budgetTips.text: The mandatory guide fee for Concepción ($25) is per group, not per person. Team up with other travellers to split the cost, as most hostels help organise this.

budgetTips.title: Ferry tickets in córdobas
budgetTips.text: Pay for ferry tickets in córdobas, not dollars, because the exchange rate at the ticket office favours córdobas. The ferry costs about 50 córdobas each way.

budgetTips.title: Bring supplies from the mainland
budgetTips.text: Everything on the island costs 20–30% more due to ferry transport. Stock up on sunscreen, snacks, and toiletries in Rivas or Granada before crossing.

practicalInfo.title: Entry & Visas
items: No additional entry requirements for Ometepe, as it is part of Nicaragua
Carry your passport on the ferry, as there are occasional police checks on board
The CA-4 visa covers Nicaragua, Guatemala, Honduras, and El Salvador for 90 days

practicalInfo.title: Health & Safety
items: Medical facilities on Ometepe are very basic, and serious injuries require evacuation to the mainland
Travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage is essential for volcano hiking
Bring all medication you might need, as pharmacies on the island are limited and poorly stocked

practicalInfo.title: Getting Around
items: Scooter rental ($15–20/day) is the best option, as the island is too large to walk between attractions
Roads are paved on the main route but deteriorate to dirt tracks on the Maderas side
Local buses run between Moyogalpa and Altagracia but are infrequent, so check schedules locally

practicalInfo.title: Connectivity
items: Mobile data coverage is patchy across the island. Claro has slightly better coverage than Tigo
WiFi at hostels is slow and unreliable. Download everything you need before crossing to the island
Consider this a digital detox opportunity, as the lack of connectivity is part of the Ometepe experience

practicalInfo.title: Money
items: There is ONE ATM on the island in Moyogalpa and it frequently runs out of cash. Bring enough córdobas and dollars from the mainland
Most businesses prefer cash. A few tourist-oriented places accept cards but do not rely on it
US dollars are accepted at some businesses but the rate is poor. Pay in córdobas whenever possible

practicalInfo.title: Packing Tips
items: Sturdy hiking boots for the volcanoes, sandals for everything else
Headlamp (essential for pre-dawn volcano starts), reusable water bottle, and a dry bag for lake activities
Insect repellent with DEET, as mosquitoes are present, especially near the lagoons and at dusk

culturalTips.title: Respect the Island
culturalTips.text: Ometepe is a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Treat the environment with care: pack out all rubbish, stay on marked trails, and do not disturb wildlife. The monkeys and birds are wild animals, not tourist attractions.

culturalTips.title: Support the Community
culturalTips.text: Ometepe is one of the poorest regions in Nicaragua. Stay at locally-owned fincas and guesthouses, eat at family comedores, and hire local guides. Your spending directly supports island families.

culturalTips.title: Photography with Permission
culturalTips.text: Always ask before photographing locals, especially indigenous communities and children. The island feels remote and traditional, so respect this by not treating residents as subjects for your social media.

culturalTips.title: Spanish is Essential
culturalTips.text: English is almost nonexistent outside a few tourist hostels. Basic Spanish is essential for navigating the island, ordering food, and communicating with your volcano guide. A phrasebook or translation app is vital.

culturalTips.title: Island Time
culturalTips.text: Ometepe operates on its own schedule. Ferries may be late, restaurants may be slow, and the ATM may be empty. This is not a place to rush. Embrace the rhythm and your stress will evaporate.

culturalTips.title: Volcano Safety
culturalTips.text: Both volcanoes are serious undertakings. Concepción is an 8–10 hour hike with significant altitude gain. Never hike without the mandatory local guide. Turn back if weather deteriorates, as the volcanoes create their own micro-weather systems.
